Lesson overview:
- Level: A1 General English
- Unit: MODULE 1. FIRST CONTACT & PERSONAL IDENTITY
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: You Must Behave
- Materials: vocabulary cards, audio, reading handout
Warm-up: say one word you already know for this topic.
Recycles imperatives from Lesson 1.17.

Answer from memory: which word belongs to this topic?
Which word belongs to this topic?
Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

rule — something you must or mustn't do. Example: It is a rule in our class.
behave — to act in a polite way. Example: Please behave in the library.
quiet — with little noise. Example: The room is quiet at night.
polite — showing good manners. Example: Be polite to the staff.
queue — to wait in a line. Example: You must queue at the desk.
phone — a telephone. Example: You mustn't use your phone here.
smoke — to use a cigarette. Example: You mustn't smoke in the building.
park — to leave a car somewhere. Example: You mustn't park in front of the door.
library — a place with books to read or borrow. Example: The library is quiet.
classroom — a room where lessons happen. Example: Our classroom is on the first floor.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• You must be quiet.
• You mustn't smoke here.
• Please queue.
• It is a rule.
• Be polite.

Grammar focus: Must / mustn’t for rules.
Use must for obligation and mustn't for prohibition: You must be quiet. You mustn't smoke here.

elements.content: Reading: read the text and answer the questions.
In the library you must be quiet and polite. You must queue at the desk. You mustn't smoke or use your phone. You mustn't park in front of the door.
